A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TACO and provide readable methods, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The change from 18 to 20 pages largely reflects reformatting and limited additions; corresponding material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original TACO segmentation experiments, baseline evaluations, ablations, computational measurements, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a quantitative comparison of encoder computational costs in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The frozen encoders, semantic-anchor co-factorization, cross-entropy penalty, temporal regularization, and FC-CLIP prompting procedure remain unchanged. The restored sigmoid explanation and reformatted pseudocode clarify the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate S4, MS3, ADE SP, AVSS, and ADE SP Semantic, retaining the same single-source, multiple-source, semantic, and negative-audio scenarios. The general versus dataset-specific word-bank evaluation is relocated, not removed.

E2.justification: Segmentation comparator membership is unchanged. The new encoder-cost comparison in v3 Table 8 includes Hamilton et al. and Park et al., already accuracy comparators in v2; v2's computational comparison in Figure 7 used the A-FC-CLIP baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds an evaluation of image, audio, and total encoder costs described as MAC counts. Existing segmentation settings remain unchanged, including 1800 optimization steps, learning rate 0.25, factorization coefficients, word-bank choices, and segmentation metrics.

E4.justification: The new MACs analysis examines the computational contributions of the image and audio encoders relative to competing systems. Existing ablations, sensitivity tests, timing analysis, and failure cases are retained; the word-bank analysis moves from v2 Section 5.1/Table 3 to v3 Appendix B/Table 7.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repetitions for experiments involving NMF decomposition and present averages and standard deviations. The uncertainty-reporting practice and existing error bars are retained.

E6.justification: Existing segmentation and ablation scores are unchanged after matching relocated tables. New Table 8 reports total encoder costs of 4.07 × 10^10 for TACO, 8.41 × 10^10 for Hamilton et al., and 6.17 × 10^10 for Park et al.; these are additional cost results, not segmentation performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, constraints, objectives, and temporal regularization in Equations 1–7 are retained. Changes to vector notation and pseudocode formatting do not introduce new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and four stated contributions retain the same substantive claims about training-free segmentation, interpretable co-factorization, FC-CLIP integration, and state-of-the-art performance. Revised image-segmentation terminology clarifies the existing task.

C2.justification: v3 adds discussion of potential multitask applicability and explains lower reported encoding cost through the efficient audio encoder despite the larger image encoder. Its conclusion explicitly identifies inference overhead as a concern in resource-constrained settings. Existing segmentation failure explanations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix J documents dataset licenses, and Appendix E identifies the audio encoder architecture in its efficiency discussion. Hyperparameters, hardware information, and the promise to release code upon acceptance were already present and remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive novelty positioning relative to trained audiovisual systems and previous NMF approaches are retained. Added terminology cross-references reuse existing citations; reference numbering and bibliographic formatting change.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose corrections, folds motivation into the method introduction, merges experimental protocol with results, and moves the word-bank discussion into Appendix B. It also removes the generic Impact Statement. Most substantive exposition remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, substantially redistributing and resizing figures and tables. Figures 2–3 and 4–5 are displayed side by side, captions are shortened, the word-bank table moves to the appendix, and Table 8 is added. All eleven figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and transparency through the repaired sigmoid explanation, dataset-license information, encoder-cost breakdown, and explicit inference-overhead limitation. The method and existing empirical evidence remain stable. The gain is limited by Table 8's inconsistent labeling: its caption says parameter sizes while the surrounding analysis describes MAC counts.
